explain.say: Sound is a wave of tiny pressure changes in the air. Noise-cancelling headphones have small microphones that listen to the noise around you, like the hum of a plane engine.

explain.say: A fast chip makes a copy of that noise wave flipped upside down, so every high-pressure peak becomes a low-pressure dip. This is called anti-noise, and the speaker plays it along with your music.

faq.q: Where are the microphones on noise-cancelling headphones?
faq.a: Most have microphones on the outside of each ear cup to hear noise before it arrives, and many also have one inside, near your ear, to check what is left and correct it.
asks: How do noise-cancelling headphones hear the noise?

faq.a: Anti-noise is a sound wave that is the exact mirror image of the noise: where the noise pushes air pressure up, the anti-noise pulls it down by the same amount.
asks: What sound do noise-cancelling headphones play?

faq.q: Why do two sound waves cancel each other?
faq.a: When two waves meet, their pressures add up. If one is at a peak exactly when the other is at a dip of the same size, they add to almost nothing, so you hear silence. This is destructive interference.

faq.q: Why can I still hear voices with noise cancelling on?
faq.a: Voices are higher pitched and change quickly, so the electronics cannot predict and copy them perfectly in time. Noise cancelling works best on steady, low sounds like engines and fans.
asks: Why doesn't noise cancelling block everything?

faq.q: Why do noise-cancelling headphones need a battery?
faq.a: The microphones, the chip that makes the anti-noise and the extra speaker work all need power. Without it, the headphones only block sound with their cushions.
asks: Do noise-cancelling headphones work without battery?

facts: Paul Lueg patented the idea of cancelling sound with sound in the 1930s.
Active noise cancellation works best on low-frequency sounds, below about 1,000 hertz.

quiz.say: What does the speaker in noise-cancelling headphones play to cancel an engine hum?
quiz.show: To cancel noise, the speaker plays…

options.show: A louder copy of the hum
options.say: A louder copy of the hum

options.show: An upside-down copy of the hum
options.say: An upside-down copy of the hum

quiz.why: A flipped copy puts a dip where each peak is, so the two waves cancel.

wrong.0: A matching copy would add to the noise and make it louder.
wrong.2: Hiss would add more noise rather than cancel it.
